title: Media Bias Measures Index
description: At the Summer Institute in Computational Social Science (SICSS-Stanford), we are developing an index of news media bias indicators for English and Spanish corpora - the goal is a program that automates the evaluation of bias in news coverage. This project started in the hopes of making computational methods more permeable and accessible for social scientists.

title: Motivated Reframing Study
collaborators: Principal Investigators: Thomas Nelson and Sunny Yang
description: Many scholars suggest that people reject information that conflicts with their political beliefs by dismissing it. We propose a different explanation - rather than simply rejecting inconvenient information, people may accept it while changing their framing of the issue, allowing them to preserve the broader belief that was challenged.

title: The human cost of machine algorithms

quote.text: Once, a scientist in Britain asked: Can machines think? He built a machine, taught it to read ghosts, and a new kind of ghost was born.

description: Social media algorithms parse through human suffering every single day. They store evidence of atrocities and human rights violations. They distill lived experience into categories and items: metadata and probabilistic signals, mechanisms for predicting topic visibility, ranking, and circulation. In a way, algorithms have taken on a life of their own. In Choi’s world, they are ghosts that make ghosts of other people, that leave ghosts behind them.

title: News Media and the Production of Elite Status in America
description: The following study examines how American news media constitutes elite status through the structure and content of coverage. Drawing on a corpus of news articles from twelve news outlets spanning 2016–2026, I construct a two-mode network connecting elite actors to news organizations. Using named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and stance detection, I map which elites get covered, how they are framed, and whether ideological outlet identity shapes both. The results speak to a broader theoretical argument in news media analysis that news visibility does not only reflect status but actively reproduces it.
